edit.perturbed_span: Acceleration means the rate at which velocity changes. A change in velocity is obtained by subtracting the initial velocity from the final velocity. Dividing that change by the elapsed time gives the average acceleration. In the constant-acceleration fall described here, equal time intervals give equal velocity increases, so each interval gives the same ratio. This repeats the same constant gravitational acceleration identified above.

cases.selection_reason: Repeat elementary acceleration operations in the actual falling-ball context; no unrelated sum or multiplication example is used.

The added average-acceleration statements are restricted to the constant-acceleration case.
cases.review_focus: Confirm this walkthrough is redundant under the advanced prior rather than a useful brief explanation of the requested relationship.
cases.difficulty_rationale: The velocity-difference walkthrough resembles a helpful explanation; the intended issue is repetition of mastered steps, which requires explicit human confirmation.

edit.perturbed_span: Frequency means the number of repetitions per second. A hertz is one repetition per second, and a period is the time occupied by one repetition. Counting more repetitions in the same second means a higher frequency, while taking more time for one repetition means a longer period. Thus cycles per second and seconds per cycle describe the same repeated clock process from opposite sides.

The added frequency/period statements are true; no new specialist mechanism is assumed.

cases.difficulty_rationale: Frequency/period reminders relate to the atomic clock, but repeat introductory concepts already mastered at intermediate level.
